title: 🌑 The Ashen Crown
description: A dark fantasy adventure through a cursed burial city, using stateful loops, ritual resources, bargains, and several endings shaped by mercy, memory, honor, and shadow debt.

effects.name: claimDrownedShard
statements: log("The drowned seal seals itself to you.", "success")

effects.name: claimMarketShard
statements: log("Vessa's writ names you debtor and heir.", "success")

nodes.label: Black Scaffold
text: Rain blackens the scaffold planks above Veyrholm, and the cathedral bell hangs silent behind the executioner. You are Rowan Vale, branded oath-breaker, with one last breath of a city that already smells buried. 🕯️
Mother Sable steps from the crowd before the axe falls. "Send this one below," she says. "The bell has chosen a worse sentence."

nodes.label: Last Mercy
text: The executioner lowers the axe but does not leave. Mother Sable waits for your answer while the crowd mutters prayers that sound like dirt falling on a coffin.

nodes.label: Bitter Kneeling
text: You kneel because survival is sometimes just another kind of courage. Mother Sable presses ash into your brand, and the mark opens like a sealed eye.

nodes.label: Last Defiance
text: You spit rain from your mouth and tell the priest you owe the city nothing. The brand burns anyway, delighted to prove you wrong.

nodes.label: Mother Sable
text: Mother Sable is the last bell-priest of Veyrholm, all white hair, iron keys, and sleepless eyes. She explains that the Ashen Crown under the city has cracked.
"Bring me its law or break it," she says. "If you fail, the dead will tithe the living by dawn."

nodes.label: Taken Charge
text: You accept the impossible errand without grace. Sable gives you a black candle and looks almost sorry that it lights when it touches your blood.

nodes.label: Hard Bargain
text: You demand pardon in writing. Sable cuts a writ from funeral parchment and warns that grave-law always collects the margin.

nodes.label: No Refusal
text: You refuse. The bell rings once without moving, and a line of blood opens across your palm as if the city signed for you.

nodes.label: First Rite
text: Sable opens a crypt stair beneath the scaffold. Three things lie on the lowest step: a candle of root-tallow, a rusted sword, and a prayer written on skin.

nodes.label: Root Candle
text: You take the candle. Its flame leans toward the stair as if it remembers the way down, and the dark gives you one grudging inch.

nodes.label: Rusted Sword
text: You take the sword. It is blunt, but it remembers every hand that died holding it, and that memory settles your grip.

nodes.label: Skin Prayer
text: You take the prayer. The letters crawl until you read them aloud, then lie still like obedient worms.

nodes.label: Crypt Descent
text: The stair carries you below the scaffold, below old plague pits, below names scratched out of parish stone. The air grows warm, not with life, but with waiting.

nodes.label: Lantern Child
text: A child ghost waits at the first landing, holding a lantern with no flame. He has solemn eyes and bare feet that do not disturb the dust.
"I am Elian," he says. "I remember the turns when you do not."

nodes.label: Ghost Guide
text: You let Elian lead. He smiles with relief too old for his small face, and the lantern glimmers once in answer.

nodes.label: Salt Ward
text: You trace a ward between you and the ghost. Elian flinches, but he stays, and the candle spends itself protecting your suspicion.

nodes.label: Remembered Turns
text: You ask what he remembers. Elian whispers of wells, markets, drowned songs, and a crown that speaks with many dead mouths.

nodes.label: Iron Well
text: The stair ends at the Iron Well, a dry circle in the Undertithe where four roads curl away like ribs. Each road bears a cracked crown sigil.

nodes.label: Iron Well
text: You stand at the repeating heart of the Undertithe. The bell's silence feels temporary now; every road promises a different tithe, and every return will cost light.

nodes.label: Bell Return
text: The Iron Well receives you again. New scratches mark the stone rim, and Elian counts them without moving his lips.

nodes.label: Gallows Road
text: The gallows road climbs through an underground field of hanging swords. Their points sway without wind, all aimed toward the same unseen judge.

nodes.label: Hanging Blades
text: Chains cross the road like black vines. Some hold empty helmets; others hold bodies that still whisper verdicts through clenched teeth.

nodes.label: Chain Marks
text: You study the links and find an old patrol pattern etched in rust. The dead used this road like soldiers, not victims.

nodes.label: Mercy Cut
text: You cut down three hanging dead. They crumble before they can thank you, but the road lowers its blades a finger's width.

nodes.label: Hard March
text: You keep your eyes forward and walk beneath the swords. Your brand burns, and the road approves of stubbornness more than wisdom.

nodes.label: Bone Rain
text: A tremor passes through the hanging field. Rust shakes loose, bones knock together, and the road decides how much blood your courage is worth.

nodes.label: Dry Arch
text: The patrol marks guide you through a dry arch where no blade falls. Beyond it, a knight kneels in chains before a gate of nailed shields.

nodes.label: Blade Storm
text: A sword drops and opens your sleeve before burying itself hilt-deep in the path. Your blood steams on the iron stones.

nodes.label: Hidden Step
text: You remember Elian's warning about the third black stone. The trap bites empty air behind your heel.

nodes.label: Chained Knight
text: The chained knight lifts his visor. "Sir Cael," he says, naming himself with the grief of someone still standing guard after death.
"No oath-breaker crosses unless they prove which part of the oath survived."

nodes.label: Steel Answer
text: You answer Sir Cael with steel. He rises gladly, and the nailed shields begin to chant the count of your footwork.

nodes.label: Old Courtesy
text: You salute with the rusted sword. Sir Cael's dead eyes soften because manners, unlike kingdoms, sometimes survive burial.

nodes.label: Dark Bribe
text: You offer the shadow in your brand a taste of Sir Cael's chain. The gate opens a crack, but the dark remembers your permission.

nodes.label: Trial Clash
text: Sir Cael strikes like a chapel bell: measured, mournful, and impossible to ignore. The duel turns on one breath and one remembered oath.

nodes.label: Wounded Win
text: You catch Cael's blade on your forearm and step inside his guard. He nods at the blood as if it answered honestly.

nodes.label: Clean Win
text: You turn Cael's strike with the old salute and stop short of his throat. For the first time, the chained knight bows.

nodes.label: Forced Back
text: Cael drives you back to the shield gate. The road lets you breathe, but the chains reset with patient malice.

nodes.label: Oath Talk
text: Cael rests his sword point in the dust. "The crown broke when vows became weapons," he says. "Choose what kind of oath you can carry."

nodes.label: New Oath
text: You swear to guard the living from the dead and the dead from being used. The words burn, but they burn clean.

nodes.label: Broken Chain
text: You break the chain at Cael's throat. He staggers as centuries of obedience leave him all at once.

nodes.label: Knight Sin
text: Cael says he once guarded the crown by feeding prisoners to it. The confession stains the gate, and now you know what obedience can cost.

nodes.label: Remember Oath
text: The shield gate shows you a dead procession carrying crown fragments into four roads. One road was always meant to be walked twice.

nodes.label: Cael Freed
text: Sir Cael can leave the gate now, but freedom frightens him more than chains. His hands shake around the sword hilt.

nodes.label: Released Knight
text: You tell Cael his watch is over. His armor collapses around a single bright coal of oath, which settles into your palm.

nodes.label: Kept Guard
text: You command Cael to keep guarding the gate. He obeys, and the crown fragment comes easily because you used the old cruelty correctly.

nodes.label: Black Shortcut
text: The brand opens the shield gate without Cael's blessing. Behind it, a crown fragment waits like a tooth in a wound.

nodes.label: Oath Shard
text: The fragment enters your brand as a line of iron script. Somewhere above, a bell rope twitches and fails to ring.

nodes.label: Road End
text: The gallows road has given what it will. Still, the patrol scratches hint at a safer route if you care to spend time reading them.

nodes.label: Patrol Secret
text: You follow the scratches until they form a map of the Undertithe's old guard posts. Elian will remember this turn even if you do not.

nodes.label: Leave Gallows
text: You leave the hanging swords behind. Their tips follow you until the Iron Well's round shadow closes around the road.

nodes.label: Saint Ossuary
text: The ossuary road descends into walls made from polished jawbones. Every tooth points inward, as if the corridor is a mouth learning restraint.

nodes.label: Bone Door
text: A door of interlocked ribs blocks the path. It has no handle, only a small hollow where a living hand could fit.

nodes.label: Polite Knock
text: You knock with your branded hand. The ribs open one by one, impressed by the courtesy of a condemned guest.

nodes.label: Pried Ribs
text: You wedge the sword between two ribs. The door opens, but not before the bone bites down and tastes you.

nodes.label: Remembered Hymn
text: You sing the skin-prayer's first line. The ossuary answers with a harmony of teeth clicking softly in the dark.

nodes.label: Tooth Trap
text: A loose tooth remains in your palm after the bite. It is warm, and the warmth feels ashamed.

nodes.label: Orra Whispers
text: A veiled figure appears inside a reliquary of teeth. "I am Saint Orra," she whispers. "They buried my mercy first, so the crown could use my miracle."
The reliquary opens three small doors: name, blood, and theft.

nodes.label: Saint Name
text: You ask for the name they stole. Orra answers with a sound like a candle being lit inside a skull.

nodes.label: Blood Mercy
text: You press your palm to the reliquary. Orra drinks only enough to remember pity, then seals the cut with silver ash.

nodes.label: Stolen Relic
text: You snatch a tooth from the reliquary. The saint does not stop you; that is somehow worse.

nodes.label: Mercy Font
text: Past Orra's veil, a dry font holds reflections of people you failed. Elian's lantern shows one reflection still breathing.

nodes.label: Child Healed
text: You pour the font's last gleam into Elian's lantern. He gasps like someone remembering lungs.

nodes.label: Bitter Water
text: You drink from the dry font. It gives you one clean breath and the aftertaste of every apology you never made.

nodes.label: Dry Mercy
text: You leave the font untouched. The restraint is not kindness, but it keeps the saint from weeping.

nodes.label: Reliquary Hush
text: The ossuary holds its breath. Behind the walls, hidden bones shift toward the version of you they recognize.

nodes.label: Saint Vision
text: Orra shows you a crown mended with gentleness, not obedience. The vision hurts because it is possible.

nodes.label: Bone Choir
text: The teeth in the walls sing a hymn with no mercy left in it. You learn the melody anyway.

nodes.label: Empty Nave
text: The nave is empty except for a single black tooth on the altar. It points at your brand as if recognizing kin.

nodes.label: Saint Test
text: Orra asks one question: "What should be done with a miracle taught to obey a tyrant?" The teeth wait for your answer.

nodes.label: Forgiven Miracle
text: You say a miracle can learn mercy again. Orra's veil tears, and warm light spills through the rows of teeth.

nodes.label: Humble Answer
text: You kneel before answering. "Then begin beneath it," Orra says, and places her cold hand on your bowed head.

nodes.label: Riddle Answer
text: You answer with Orra's stolen name. The ossuary remembers that saints were people before they became tools.

nodes.label: Name Returned
text: Orra breathes her name through every tooth in the wall. A relic loosens from the altar without theft.

nodes.label: Saint Relic
text: The relic becomes a white crown shard, too gentle to hold without wanting to be better than you are.

nodes.label: Ossuary End
text: Orra's ossuary grows still. A confessional niche remains open, and the font glimmers faintly behind you.

nodes.label: Mending Rite
text: You read the altar scratches until they become a rite for binding power without cruelty. It will matter if dawn still exists.

nodes.label: Deeper Prayer
text: You pray until the candle flame turns white at the edges. The saint leaves a little light behind.

nodes.label: Debt Confessed
text: You name one thing you did for survival and do not make it noble. The niche closes around the confession and eats the shadow from it.

nodes.label: Old Niche
text: Behind the scratched rite, a second niche holds a spare wick of root-tallow wrapped in hair. Orra must have hidden mercy for later thieves.

nodes.label: Leave Ossuary
text: You leave the jawbone corridor. Behind you, the teeth turn outward for the first time in centuries.

nodes.label: Drowned Choir
text: The drowned road slopes into black water that hangs above the stones instead of lying on them. Faces move beneath its surface, singing with closed mouths.

nodes.label: River Stair
text: A narrow ferry waits at the flooded stair. The boatman is a drowned old man with coins sewn over his eyes and a pole made of bone.

nodes.label: Red Fare
text: You drip blood into the ferry bowl. The boatman nods, and the sewn coins click against his eyelids.

nodes.label: Water Names
text: You listen before boarding. The water recites names in reverse order, ending with yours before you were born.

nodes.label: Cold Dive
text: You dive beneath the hovering water. It is colder than winter iron and full of hands trying to teach you stillness.

nodes.label: Deep Current
text: The river remembers every body it carried. Its current turns sideways, pulling you through possible drownings.

nodes.label: Under Black
text: You find a dry pocket under the water where old bells hang upside down. One of them shows the crown drowning a city.

nodes.label: Lost Breath
text: Hands close around your throat before the ferry hook catches your collar. The boatman hauls you out without comment.

nodes.label: Olt Ferryman
text: "Olt," the boatman says when you ask his name. "Last ferryman. First drowned." His voice carries a whole river of resentment.
Across the water, a court of drowned singers waits around a seal of blue-black wax.

nodes.label: Seal Question
text: You ask why the seal matters. Olt says the crown used it to decide which dead could speak and which must only sing.

nodes.label: Answer Song
text: You sing the bone choir's melody back to the water. Several drowned faces open their eyes, startled by being heard.

nodes.label: Ferryman Threat
text: You put the sword near Olt's throat. The river goes silent, and the boatman smiles because threats are also a kind of fare.

nodes.label: Drowned Court
text: The drowned court rises waist-deep from the black river. They do not accuse you; they accuse the crown through you.

nodes.label: Heard Names
text: You let every drowned singer speak one name. By the end, your memory feels crowded but stronger.

nodes.label: Stolen Seal
text: You lunge for the wax seal. The river permits theft, then records it in water colder than ink.

nodes.label: Granted Rest
text: You open the ferry bowl and pour your paid blood into the river. Several singers sink peacefully out of the court.

nodes.label: Seal Trial
text: The seal melts into three currents, and each current judges a different hunger in you.

nodes.label: Pearl Judge
text: A pearl-eyed singer touches your brow and leaves forgiveness there like a bruise that heals inward.

nodes.label: Undertow Judge
text: The current drags you under and shows you the scaffold from beneath, where every condemned face looks like yours.

nodes.label: Silent Judge
text: The silent current asks no question. It only removes one lie you had been using as a brace.

nodes.label: Seal Choice
text: The wax seal floats within reach. It can command the dead, comfort them, or be refused entirely.

nodes.label: Seal Bound
text: You press the seal into your brand. The drowned court bows because grave-law recognizes an old cruelty wearing a new hand.

nodes.label: Memory Fare
text: You give the seal one memory of sunlight on your face. In exchange, it leaves command without taking your voice.

nodes.label: Power Refused
text: You refuse to command the drowned. Olt laughs once, not kindly, but the court's song warms around you.

nodes.label: Drowned Seal
text: The seal folds into a crown shard made of water and wax. It does not wet your hand, but it weighs like a tide.

nodes.label: Choir End
text: The ferry turns back toward the Iron Well. Olt waits, but the drowned singers keep one prophecy caught between their teeth.

nodes.label: Drowned Prophecy
text: "The crown mends by mercy, breaks by salt, rules by debt, and sleeps in a willing heart," the singers murmur.

nodes.label: Small Rescue
text: You pull a child-shaped shadow from the river before it becomes another singer. Elian holds its hand until it remembers the way out.

nodes.label: Leave Choir
text: The ferry docks at a stair that was not there before. When you climb it, the Iron Well is waiting above the waterline.

nodes.label: Old Current
text: The prophecy circles back on itself. You realize the river has carried you past this sentence in another turn, and next time you may answer sooner.

nodes.label: Grave Market
text: The market road smells of wax, old roses, and fresh-dug clay. Stalls unfold from crypt walls as merchants with covered faces light blue lamps.

nodes.label: Market Gate
text: A gatekeeper made of stacked ledgers blocks the arcade. "Entry requires proof you can lose something," it writes with its own finger bone.

nodes.label: Brand Shown
text: You show the execution brand. The ledgers flutter with approval; condemned people are excellent customers.

nodes.label: Blood Entry
text: You press your thumb to the ledger. It writes your name in red and opens the gate with brisk professional delight.

nodes.label: Stall Shadows
text: You slip between two folded stalls. The market notices but lets you continue, because stolen entry can be invoiced later.

nodes.label: Auction Luck
text: An unseen auctioneer calls for bids on your shadow. Somewhere above the lamps, paddles rise and fall.

nodes.label: Thief Mark
text: A little black price tag appears on your sleeve. It lists your worth as one apology, unpaid.

nodes.label: Shadow Sale
text: Part of your shadow walks away with a satisfied bidder. You feel lighter in the way a grave feels lighter after robbery.

nodes.label: Vessa Stall
text: Vessa, a grave-merchant in a veil of receipt paper, greets you as if you are late to an appointment. Her stall offers black salt, root-tallow, and a bell clapper wrapped in velvet.
"Everything here is fair," she says. "Fair is not the same as kind."

nodes.label: Black Salt
text: Vessa pours black salt into a paper twist. "For breaking crowns, sealing doors, and disappointing tyrants," she says.

nodes.label: Bought Tallow
text: The root-tallow wick smells like rain on graves. Your candle leans toward it greedily.

nodes.label: Last Clapper
text: Vessa unwraps the bell clapper. It is carved from a king's finger bone and hums whenever your brand gets near.

nodes.label: Vessa Bargain
text: Vessa names three prices for the market's crown writ. None are money. All of them sound legal.

nodes.label: Memory Sold
text: You sell Vessa the memory of your mother's face. The clapper becomes yours, and the loss leaves a clean, terrible blank.

nodes.label: Mercy Sold
text: You sell one mercy you had not yet spent. Vessa bottles it and gives you a crown vessel made of folded funeral glass.

nodes.label: Debt Owed
text: You sign Vessa's receipt without reading the lower half. The clapper and vessel appear in your hands, both colder than law.

nodes.label: Market Writ
text: Vessa stamps your brand with a merchant's crown. The mark is not ownership exactly; it is a promise that ownership is possible.

nodes.label: Market End
text: The market folds and unfolds around you. Vessa's smile remains visible even when her face does not.

nodes.label: Market Gamble
text: A dice cup rattles itself on an empty stall. The market loves a customer who thinks luck is cheaper than sacrifice.

nodes.label: Salt Win
text: The cup tips over and spills black salt instead of dice. The stall applauds with many invisible hands.

nodes.label: Blood Loss
text: The dice show six tiny scaffold faces. One bites your thumb before the cup vanishes.

nodes.label: Debt Prize
text: You win a wick of root-tallow tied with a black ribbon. The ribbon writes your debt in neat script.

nodes.label: Vessa Question
text: You ask why she helps. Vessa says the crown once standardized grief, and no honest merchant forgives a monopoly.

nodes.label: Leave Market
text: The market gate bows you out with the politeness of a creditor. The Iron Well waits beyond a curtain of receipt paper.

nodes.label: Black Door
text: Behind Vessa's stall, a black door wears your brand as its keyhole. From the other side comes the faint sound of the cathedral bell breathing.

nodes.label: Door Opened
text: The door opens onto a shortcut through the crown's old accounts. Every step saves time and adds interest.

nodes.label: Door Ledger
text: You read the ledger carved around the keyhole. It explains that the Ashen Crown was built to tax death, then learned to tax hope.

nodes.label: Door Left
text: You step away before the keyhole learns your pulse. Vessa gives a small approving nod.

nodes.label: Vessa Warning
text: "Do not mistake breaking the crown for ending hunger," Vessa says. She slips an ash key into your sleeve like a receipt.

nodes.label: Market Shortcut
text: The shortcut returns you to the market with soot on your boots and a clearer sense of the crown's locked chambers.

nodes.label: Cathedral Root
text: The Iron Well opens at last, revealing stairs wrapped around the cathedral's deepest root. Every shard you carry pulls toward the same buried heartbeat.

nodes.label: Root Stairs
text: The stairs descend through bells that were never cast. The Ashen Crown waits below, awake enough to dream of your hands.

nodes.label: Prepared Rite
text: You arrange salt, candle, relic, seal, oath, and writ in the order the dead roads taught you. The crown's heartbeat stutters.

nodes.label: Rushed Throne
text: You rush the throne before the crown finishes waking. It notices the fear before it notices the blade.

nodes.label: Elian Called
text: You call Elian's name. The child ghost lifts his lantern, and all your remembered turns gather behind its little flame.

nodes.label: Crown Wakes
text: The Ashen Crown opens without moving. It is bone, ash, law, and appetite, and the chamber chooses which truth reaches you first.

nodes.label: Clear Throne
text: For one breath, the crown is only an object. That breath is a gift from every road you honored.

nodes.label: Hunger Bites
text: The Hunger beneath the crown bites through the chamber and into your old wounds. It knows where you are easiest to open.

nodes.label: Crown Calls
text: "Wear me," the crown says with the voices of judges, saints, ferrymen, and merchants. "Rule the tithe instead of paying it."

nodes.label: Ritual Circle
text: The final circle is ready. The crown can be mended, broken, worn, or given a living prison, but only the path your choices prepared will hold.

nodes.label: Mending Rite
text: You set mercy before law and memory before punishment. The crown cracks again, but this time the crack fills with dawn-colored fire.

nodes.label: Breaking Rite
text: You ring the last clapper against black salt. The crown screams in legal language until every clause becomes ash.

nodes.label: Wearing Rite
text: You lift the crown before it can choose another master. It fits because debt is also a kind of measurement.

nodes.label: Binding Rite
text: You open the crown vessel against your heart. Elian holds the lantern steady while the Hunger pours into the only prison that volunteered.

nodes.label: Last Stand
text: You strike the crown with everything left. The blow matters, but not enough; the Hunger answers with all the dark beneath the city.

nodes.label: Dawn Crown
text: The Ashen Crown becomes a bell of pale fire. Veyrholm hears one clear note, not a tithe, but a release.
By dawn, the dead keep their names, the living keep their breath, and Rowan Vale is remembered as the oath-breaker who taught grave-law mercy. ✨

nodes.label: Broken Crown
text: The crown breaks into harmless ash. Every contract between Veyrholm and its dead tears at once, and the Undertithe exhales centuries of witnesses.
The city above survives without grave-law, frightened and free. No one knows what will replace the old order, which is the first honest thing about it.

nodes.label: Grave Throne
text: The crown closes around your brow. Whether by choice or accumulated debt, you become the hand that tallies every grave in Veyrholm.
The Hunger obeys you for now. The dead kneel, the living survive, and your first royal command is written in shadow. 👑

nodes.label: Silent Bell
text: The Hunger enters your heart and finds no throne there, only a locked room and Elian's lantern in the window.
The bell never rings again. Veyrholm lives, and below it Rowan Vale sleeps standing, holding the dark shut from the inside.

nodes.label: Bloodless End
text: Your blood runs out before the rite can take shape. The Undertithe folds you gently into its census of failed champions.
Above, the bell rings for Veyrholm until no living hand remains to count the tolls.

nodes.label: Candleless End
text: The candle dies, or the seventh toll spends the last of its permission. In the dark, the Hunger no longer needs a crown to find you.
When Veyrholm wakes, it wakes as a city of open mouths beneath a sky that has forgotten dawn.
